ja: だいきゅうじゅうろくかい

p.src: Our story continues: Jia Lian took the counterfeit jade and stalked angrily out to the study. When the man saw the dark look on Jia Lian’s face, his courage failed him; he hurriedly rose to greet him. He was just about to speak when Jia Lian sneered, “What brazen nerve, you damned scoundrel! Do you know what sort of place this is, that you dare come here playing tricks?” Turning his head, he demanded, “Where are the pages?” Several pages outside answered in unison with a roar like thunder. Jia Lian ordered, “Fetch a rope and bind him. When Master returns, we shall question him properly and send him to the magistrate’s office.” Again the pages answered together, “The rope is ready.” Yet despite their words, none of them moved. The man was already terrified out of his wits. Seeing this display and knowing he could not escape justice, he had no choice but to kneel and knock his head before Jia Lian, crying over and over, “My venerable lord, please don’t be angry! I was driven to desperation by poverty and, in a moment of folly, devised this shameless trade. I borrowed money to have that jade made. I dare not ask anything for it now; let me offer it to the young gentlemen of the house as a plaything.” When he had finished, he repeatedly knocked his head on the floor. Jia Lian spat at him. “You reckless fool! Do you imagine this household covets that wretched trinket of yours, which would not even rot away?” In the midst of the uproar, Lai Da came in and said to Jia Lian with an ingratiating smile, “Please calm yourself, Second Master. He is a worthless creature. Spare him and make him clear out.” “He is truly detestable,” said Jia Lian. While Lai Da tried by every means to placate Jia Lian, those outside shouted, “You muddle-headed son of a dog, why don’t you kowtow to the master and Steward Lai? Clear out at once! Are you waiting for a kick in the chest?” The man hastily kowtowed twice, then fled in abject terror. From then on, the streets buzzed with the tale that “Jia Baoyu had brought forth a ‘fake Baoyu.’”

p.src: Now Jia Zheng returned that day from paying calls. As the Lantern Festival was at hand, everyone feared upsetting him and, since the incident was already past, none was willing to report it. The household had been occupied for a long while with the affairs following Consort Yuan’s death, and lately Baoyu had fallen ill. Though custom called for a family feast, no one was in the mood, and nothing occurred worth recording. On the seventeenth day of the first month, while Lady Wang was eagerly awaiting Wang Ziteng’s arrival in the capital, Xifeng came in and reported, “Second Master heard a rumor outside today that our elder lord, while hurrying to the capital, died on the road little more than two hundred li from the city. Have you heard of it, madam?” Lady Wang exclaimed in alarm, “I have heard nothing. Master said nothing about it last night either. Where exactly did he hear this?” “They say he heard it at Lord Zhang’s residence in the Privy Council,” replied Xifeng. Lady Wang sat stunned for a long while, tears already streaming down her face. Wiping them away, she said, “When Lian returns, have him make thorough inquiries and come tell me the truth.” Xifeng assented and left. Lady Wang could not help weeping in private, grieving for her daughter, mourning her younger brother, and worrying over Baoyu as well. Misfortunes had come one after another; unable to bear so many distressing events, she began to suffer pains in her chest. Then Jia Lian returned after establishing the facts and reported, “Uncle was exhausted from hurrying on his journey and happened to catch a chill. When he reached Shilitun, a physician was summoned to treat him. Unfortunately, there was no skilled doctor in that place. The wrong medicine was prescribed, and a single dose killed him. But I do not know whether his family has arrived there yet.” At this, Lady Wang was overcome with grief. The pain in her chest grew so severe that she could no longer sit upright, and she had Caiyun and the others help her onto the kang. Still struggling to hold herself together, she told Jia Lian to report to Jia Zheng: “Pack at once and go meet them there. Help settle all the necessary affairs, then return immediately and tell us what has happened. That will set your wife’s mind at ease.” Jia Lian dared not disobey. He took leave of Jia Zheng and set out. Jia Zheng had already learned the news and was deeply distressed. He also knew that since losing the jade, Baoyu had remained dazed and confused despite all medical treatment, while Lady Wang was now suffering from chest pains. That year coincided with the metropolitan review of officials, and the Ministry of Works recommended Jia Zheng in the first class. In the second month, the Ministry of Personnel presented him for an imperial audience. Mindful of Jia Zheng’s diligence, frugality, and prudence, the Emperor appointed him Grain Intendant of Jiangxi. That same day Jia Zheng expressed his gratitude for the imperial favor and submitted the date of his departure. Although many relatives and friends came to congratulate him, Jia Zheng had no heart for social courtesies. He thought only of the unrest in his household, yet dared not delay his departure. Just as he was at a complete loss what to do, word came from Grandmother Jia’s quarters: “The Old Lady requests the master’s presence.”

p.src: Jia Zheng hurried inside and found Lady Wang there despite her illness. He paid his respects to Grandmother Jia. Grandmother Jia told him to sit down and said, “You will soon leave to take up your post. I have much to say to you, but I do not know whether you will heed me.” As she spoke, tears fell from her eyes. Jia Zheng rose hastily and said, “Please command me as you wish, Mother. How could your son dare disobey?” Grandmother Jia said through her sobs, “I am eighty-one this year, and now you are going away to serve in the provinces. Yet with your elder brother at home, you cannot plead an aged parent as grounds for declining the post. Once you leave, the only one dear to me will be Baoyu, and he has fallen so grievously ill that he has lost his senses. Heaven knows what will become of him. Yesterday I sent Lai Sheng’s wife to find someone to tell Baoyu’s fortune. The diviner proved remarkably accurate. He said Baoyu must marry a woman whose destiny belongs to the element of gold, so that the joyful occasion may dispel his illness; otherwise, I fear his life cannot be saved. I know you do not believe such things, so I summoned you to discuss it. Your wife is here as well. You two may discuss it together: do you want Baoyu to recover, or will you simply abandon him to his fate?” Jia Zheng answered with a deferential smile, “Mother loved me so dearly in years past. Could I, as a father, possibly fail to love my own son? It is only because Baoyu refuses to better himself that I am often angry with him; my disappointment springs solely from wishing he would amount to something. Since Mother wishes to see him married, as indeed is proper, how could I oppose you and show myself indifferent to him? Now that Baoyu is ill, I too am deeply concerned. But since Mother would not allow him to see me, I dared say nothing. I must see for myself what kind of illness Baoyu has.” Lady Wang saw Jia Zheng’s eyes redden as he spoke and knew that he truly loved the boy, so she told Xiren to help Baoyu in. When Baoyu saw his father, Xiren prompted him to pay his respects, and he did so. Jia Zheng saw that his face was gaunt, his gaze vacant, and his manner almost demented. He had Baoyu helped back inside and thought, “I myself am nearing sixty, and now I have been appointed to a provincial post, with no knowing how many years it will be before I return. If the boy should indeed die, then first, I shall be old and without an heir; though I have a grandson, that is still one generation removed. Second, Baoyu is Mother’s dearest treasure, and if anything befalls him, will not my guilt be heavier still?” He glanced at Lady Wang, whose eyes brimmed with tears, then thought again of his own predicament. Rising once more, he said, “At Mother’s great age, you spare no effort for your grandson. How could your son dare oppose you? Whatever Mother decides shall be done. But I wonder whether the matter has been fully explained to Aunt Xue?”

p.src: Lady Wang replied, “My sister agreed long ago. It has not been mentioned lately only because Pan’s case has yet to be settled.” Jia Zheng said, “That is the first difficulty. How can the sister marry while her brother is in prison? Moreover, although the Imperial Consort’s death does not prohibit marriages, Baoyu must observe nine months of mourning for his married sister, so it is difficult for him to wed at present. And the date of my departure has already been reported to the throne; I dare not delay. How can everything be managed in these few days?” Grandmother Jia reflected for a moment. “What you say is indeed true. But if we wait until all these matters are past, his father will have left. And what shall we do if his illness grows worse by the day? We shall have to set aside some formalities and arrange it at once.” Having settled her plan, she said, “If you will arrange it for him, I have a way to ensure that none of these obstacles causes trouble. Your wife and I will go personally to entreat my niece on that side. As for Pan, I shall ask Ke to tell him that this is to save Baoyu’s life and that everyone must make allowances; naturally he will agree. Of course, a wedding during mourning is truly impermissible. Besides, with Baoyu ill, we cannot have him consummate a marriage. This is merely to counteract his illness with a joyful event. Both families consent, and the children are already linked by the affinity of gold and jade, so there is no need to compare their horoscopes. We shall choose an auspicious day and exchange the betrothal gifts in a manner befitting our family’s station. Then we shall promptly choose a wedding day. We shall dispense with all drums and music and instead follow palace custom: she will be brought here in an eight-bearer sedan preceded by twelve pairs of lanterns; they will bow in the wedding hall according to southern custom, then sit together on the bridal bed while the bed-curtains are strewn with auspicious tokens. Will that not count as a marriage? Baochai is sensible and discerning, so there is nothing to worry about. And Xiren is there too; she is a thoroughly dependable girl. It would be better still to have another sensible person constantly advising him. She also gets along well with Baochai. Besides, my niece once said that a monk had pronounced upon Baochai’s golden locket, saying that its destined match would be one who possessed jade. Who can say that once Baochai comes here, her golden locket may not draw Baoyu’s lost jade back to him? If from then on he improves day by day, will that not be a blessing for us all? For now, we need only prepare and furnish the rooms at once. You must assign those rooms. We shall invite no relatives or friends and hold no banquet. Once Baoyu has recovered and the mourning period is over, we can give a feast and invite everyone. Done this way, there will be time enough for everything. You will also see the young couple settled and can leave with an easy mind.” Jia Zheng was reluctant, but since Grandmother Jia had decided, he dared not disobey. Forcing a smile, he said, “Mother’s plan is excellent and most appropriate.

p.src: We must, however, order everyone in the household not to make such a commotion that the news becomes known both within and without, for that could cause serious trouble. I fear Aunt Xue may be unwilling. But if she truly agrees, then we can only proceed according to Mother’s plan.” Grandmother Jia said, “Leave my niece to me. You may go.” Jia Zheng assented and withdrew, feeling deeply uneasy. With so much to do before taking up his post—collecting his credentials from the ministry, dealing with candidates recommended by relatives and friends, and attending to an endless succession of social obligations—he ultimately left Baoyu’s affair entirely to Grandmother Jia, Lady Wang, and Xifeng. He merely assigned to Baoyu the large compound of more than twenty rooms behind the Hall of Glorious Felicity, beside Lady Wang’s inner apartments, and concerned himself with nothing else. After Grandmother Jia had settled the plan, she sent someone to inform him, and Jia Zheng merely said that it was very well. But that belongs to what follows.

p.src: Now, after Baoyu had seen Jia Zheng, Xiren helped him back onto the kang in the inner room. As Jia Zheng was still outside, no one dared speak to Baoyu, and he soon fell into a heavy, befuddled sleep. Baoyu did not hear a single word of what Grandmother Jia and Jia Zheng said. Xiren and the others, however, listened quietly and heard everything clearly. They had heard some rumors before, but those had been vague and insubstantial; and since Baochai had not come, they had begun to think there might be some truth in them. Only after hearing these words today did Xiren feel that everything had become clear and settled, and she was pleased. She thought, “Those above us have indeed judged wisely. This is truly a fitting match. It is good fortune for me as well. Once she comes, I shall be able to lay down many of my burdens. But this young master has room in his heart for no one but Miss Lin. Luckily he did not hear any of this; if he learned of it, there is no telling what sort of turmoil he would cause.” At this thought, Xiren’s joy turned to sorrow, and she reflected, “What is to be done about this? Grandmother and Her Ladyship know nothing of what is in their hearts. In their delight, they may tell him of it, hoping that the news will cure his illness. But if his feelings are still what they were—when he first met Miss Lin, he tried to fling down and smash his jade; and that summer in the garden he mistook me for her and confided so many secret thoughts to me; later, when Zijuan made one teasing remark, he wept as though he would die. If they now tell him that he is to marry Miss Bao and cast Miss Lin aside, it might be safe only if he remains wholly insensible. Should he understand even a little, I fear the marriage will not dispel his illness but hasten his death! If I still fail to explain matters plainly, would I not be bringing ruin upon three people at once?” Having made up her mind, Xiren waited until Jia Zheng had gone, told Qiuwen to watch over Baoyu, and came out of the inner room. She went to Lady Wang’s side and quietly asked her to come speak in the room behind Grandmother Jia’s quarters. Grandmother Jia merely supposed that Baoyu had sent some message and paid no heed, continuing to plan how the betrothal gifts should be exchanged and how the wedding should be arranged.

p.src: When Xiren and Lady Wang reached the back room, Xiren knelt down and began to weep. Not knowing what this meant, Lady Wang took her by the hand and said, “Why are you doing this when all was well? If you have suffered some grievance, get up and tell me.” Xiren said, “This is not something a servant ought to say, but now there is no other way.” “Take your time and tell me,” said Lady Wang. Xiren said, “Grandmother and Your Ladyship have chosen Miss Bao as Baoyu’s bride, and naturally that is an excellent match. But I have been wondering: in Your Ladyship’s opinion, is Baoyu closer to Miss Bao or to Miss Lin?” Lady Wang replied, “Those two have been together since childhood, so Baoyu is somewhat closer to Miss Lin.” “It is more than somewhat,” said Xiren. She then recounted one by one how things had always stood between Baoyu and Daiyu, adding, “Your Ladyship witnessed all these things with your own eyes. Only what he said that summer is something I have never dared tell anyone.” Lady Wang took Xiren by the hand and said, “I had already noticed something of it from their outward behavior. What you have told me today makes it still clearer. But he must have heard what the master said just now. How did he look?” Xiren replied, “Nowadays, if someone speaks to Baoyu, he smiles; if no one speaks to him, he sleeps. So in fact he heard none of what was said earlier.” Lady Wang said, “Then what are we to do about this?” Xiren replied, “I have said what I had to say. Your Ladyship must still tell Grandmother and devise some perfectly safe plan.” Lady Wang then said, “In that case, go back to your duties. The room is full of people now, so do not mention this for the time being. When I find an opportunity, I shall report it to Grandmother, and then we shall decide what to do.” With that, she returned to Grandmother Jia’s side.

Lady Wang replied, “Those two have been together since childhood, so Baoyu is somewhat closer to Miss Lin.”
“It is more than somewhat,” said Xiren.
She then recounted one by one how things had always stood between Baoyu and Daiyu, adding, “Your Ladyship witnessed all these things with your own eyes.
Only what he said that summer is something I have never dared tell anyone.”
Lady Wang took Xiren by the hand and said, “I had already noticed something of it from their outward behavior.
What you have told me today makes it still clearer.
But he must have heard what the master said just now. How did he look?”
Xiren replied, “Nowadays, if someone speaks to Baoyu, he smiles; if no one speaks to him, he sleeps.
So in fact he heard none of what was said earlier.”
Lady Wang said, “Then what are we to do about this?”
Xiren replied, “I have said what I had to say. Your Ladyship must still tell Grandmother and devise some perfectly safe plan.”

Lady Wang then said, “In that case, go back to your duties. The room is full of people now, so do not mention this for the time being. When I find an opportunity, I shall report it to Grandmother, and then we shall decide what to do.”
With that, she returned to Grandmother Jia’s side.

p.src: Grandmother Jia was discussing matters with Xifeng when Lady Wang entered, and she asked, “What did that girl Xiren say? Why all this secrecy?” Taking the opportunity afforded by her question, Lady Wang gave Grandmother Jia a detailed account of what was troubling Baoyu. After hearing her out, Grandmother Jia remained silent for a long while. Lady Wang and Xifeng also said no more. At last Grandmother Jia sighed. “Anything else could be dealt with easily. There is no particular difficulty as far as that girl Lin is concerned, but if Baoyu truly feels this way, it puts us in a terrible quandary.” Xifeng thought for a moment and said, “It need not be difficult. I have an idea, though I do not know whether Aunt will agree to it.” Lady Wang said, “If you have an idea, tell it to the Old Lady. We women can discuss it together and decide what to do.” “In my view,” said Xifeng, “there is only one way to manage this—a substitution.” “How would this substitution work?” asked Grandmother Jia. Xifeng replied, “Whether Brother Bao is in his right mind or not, we should make a great show of announcing that the Master has decided to marry Miss Lin to him. Then we shall see how he reacts. If he takes no notice at all, there will be no need for any substitution. But if he shows signs of being pleased, we shall have to go to a great deal of trouble.” Lady Wang asked, “Even if he is pleased, what do you propose to do?” Xifeng went to Lady Wang’s side and whispered the whole plan in her ear. Lady Wang nodded several times, smiled, and said, “Very well, then.” Grandmother Jia asked, “What mischief are you two plotting? Tell me exactly what you mean!” Afraid that Grandmother Jia might misunderstand and give the game away, Xifeng also whispered the plan into her ear. Sure enough, Grandmother Jia did not understand at first, so Xifeng laughingly added a few words of explanation. Grandmother Jia laughed. “That should do very well, though it will be terribly hard on that girl Bao. And what if the story gets out and that girl Lin hears of it?” Xifeng replied, “This is meant for Baoyu’s ears alone. No one outside is to mention a word of it, so how could anyone else know?” While they were speaking, a maid came in with the message, “Second Master Lian has returned.” Lady Wang, afraid that Grandmother Jia might question him about the matter, gave Xifeng a meaningful look. Xifeng went to meet Jia Lian, signaling to him with a movement of her lips, and the two of them went to Lady Wang’s room to wait. When Lady Wang came in a little later, she found Xifeng’s eyes already red and swollen from weeping. After paying his respects, Jia Lian gave a full account of his journey to Shilitun to arrange Wang Ziteng’s funeral, then said, “By an imperial act of grace, he was granted an official rank in the Grand Secretariat and the posthumous title Duke Wenqin. His clansmen were ordered to escort his coffin back to his native place, with the local officials along the route instructed to assist them. They set out yesterday, and his family has gone south with them.

p.src: Aunt asked me to return and convey her respects and good wishes. She said she had never imagined that she would be unable to come to the capital, and that there was so much she had been unable to say. She has heard that my elder brother-in-law is coming to the capital, and if she meets him on the road, she will ask him to come here and tell us everything in detail.” Lady Wang’s grief upon hearing all this need hardly be described. Xifeng comforted her for a while and said, “Please rest a little, Madam. We can discuss Baoyu’s affairs again this evening.” With that, she returned to her own rooms with Jia Lian, told him about the plan, and instructed him to send servants to prepare the bridal chamber. No more need be said of this.

p.src: One day after breakfast, Daiyu took Zijuan with her to visit Grandmother Jia, partly to pay her respects and partly to relieve her own melancholy. After leaving the Xiaoxiang Lodge and walking a short distance, she suddenly remembered that she had forgotten her handkerchief. She sent Zijuan back to fetch it while she herself walked slowly on and waited for her. Just as she reached the rocks beyond Qinfang Bridge, at the place where she and Baoyu had once buried the fallen flowers, she suddenly heard someone sobbing there. Daiyu stopped to listen, but could neither identify the voice nor make out the words being muttered through the tears. Much puzzled, she slowly approached. When she drew near, she saw a thick-browed, large-eyed maid crying there. Before seeing her, Daiyu had supposed that one of the senior maids of the household, burdened by some secret sorrow, had come there to give vent to her feelings. But when she saw this girl, she found the notion amusing and thought, “What deep feelings could such a simpleton possess? She must be some drudge from one of the rooms who has been mistreated by a senior maid.” She looked more closely but did not recognize her. When the maid saw Daiyu approaching, she dared not continue crying, but rose and wiped away her tears. Daiyu asked, “Why are you grieving here when nothing seems to be wrong?” At these words the maid began to weep again. “Miss Lin, please judge whether this is fair. I knew nothing about what they had been saying. I only let one wrong remark slip, and surely that was no reason for my elder sister to hit me!” Daiyu did not understand what she meant and asked with a smile, “Who is this elder sister of yours?” “Sister Zhenzhu,” replied the maid. Only then did Daiyu realize that she belonged to Grandmother Jia’s household, and she asked, “What is your name?” “My name is Silly Girl,” the maid replied. Daiyu smiled and asked again, “Why did your sister hit you? What was it that you said wrong?” “Why, it was about our Second Master Bao marrying Miss Bao,” replied the maid. When Daiyu heard these words, it was as though a thunderbolt had struck, and her heart began to pound wildly. After steadying herself a little, she called to the maid, “Come over here with me.” The maid followed Daiyu to the secluded corner where the peach blossoms had been buried. Daiyu then asked, “Why did she hit you over Second Master Bao marrying Miss Bao?” Silly Girl replied, “Our Old Lady, Madam, and Second Mistress Lian discussed it together. Since our Master is about to leave, they said they should hurry over to consult Aunt and bring Miss Bao here as the bride.”

p.src: “The first thing is to arrange some joyous occasion to counteract Second Master Bao’s illness, and the second—” Here she glanced at Daiyu and smiled before continuing, “Once that has been hurried through, they must find a husband’s family for Miss Lin.” Daiyu was already too stunned to speak. The maid went on, “I didn’t know what arrangements they had made. They told everyone not to make a commotion, for fear Miss Bao might hear and feel embarrassed. All I did was say to Sister Xiren in Second Master Bao’s room, ‘Tomorrow will be livelier than ever: there’ll be Miss Bao and also Second Mistress Bao. What are we to call them both?’ Miss Lin, tell me, how did those words offend Sister Zhenzhu? She came over and slapped me, saying I was talking nonsense and disobeying orders from above, and that she would have me driven out. How was I to know why those above had forbidden anyone to speak of it? None of you told me, yet she struck me.” At this, she began crying again.

p.src: Daiyu now felt as though oil, sauce, sugar, and vinegar had all been poured together in her heart; amid the sweetness, bitterness, sourness, and saltiness, she could no longer tell what she felt. After a pause, she said in a trembling voice, “You must stop talking nonsense. If you say such things again and someone hears you, you will be struck again. Go now.” With that, she turned to make her way back to the潇湘馆. Her body seemed to weigh a thousand catties, while her feet felt as though they were treading on cotton and had already gone limp. She could only advance slowly, one step at a time. She had walked for what seemed an age without reaching Qinfang Bridge, for her legs had failed her. Besides walking slowly, she was dazed and bewildered; letting her feet carry her around by another way added several hundred paces to her journey. When at last she reached Qinfang Bridge, she unconsciously began walking back along the embankment. Zijuan returned with the handkerchief, but Daiyu was nowhere to be seen. As she looked around, she saw Daiyu, white as snow, swaying unsteadily with a fixed stare, wandering first one way and then another. She also saw a maid walking on ahead, but the girl was too far away for her to make out who it was. Alarmed and perplexed, she hurried over and asked softly, “Why are you going back again, miss? Where are you going?” Daiyu heard her only vaguely and answered at random, “I am going to ask Baoyu!” Zijuan could make neither head nor tail of this and had no choice but to support her to Grandmother Jia’s quarters.

p.src: When Daiyu reached the entrance to Grandmother Jia’s quarters, her mind cleared a little. Turning and seeing Zijuan supporting her, she stopped and asked, “What have you come for?” Zijuan replied with a smile, “I went to fetch the handkerchief. A moment ago I saw you by the bridge and hurried over to ask you where you were going, but you paid no attention.” Daiyu smiled. “I thought you had come to see Second Master Bao. Why else would you be walking this way?” Seeing how confused she was, Zijuan realized that Daiyu must have heard something from the maid, but could only nod and smile faintly. Yet inwardly she feared what might happen when Daiyu saw Baoyu: he was already raving like a fool, and now she too was in such a trance. What if, in a moment, they said something improper? Though these thoughts troubled her, she dared not oppose Daiyu and could only help her inside. Strangely, Daiyu no longer seemed as weak as before. Without waiting for Zijuan to lift the curtain, she raised it herself and went in. All was perfectly still. Grandmother Jia was taking her midday nap. Some of the maids had slipped away to amuse themselves, some were dozing, and others were attending the old lady. Xiren alone heard the curtain rustle. She came out of the room, saw Daiyu, and invited her in: “Please come inside and sit down, miss.” Daiyu asked with a smile, “Is Second Master Bao at home?” Not knowing what lay behind the question, Xiren was about to answer when she saw Zijuan behind Daiyu pursing her lips toward her, pointing at Daiyu, and waving her hand. Xiren did not understand what she meant, but dared not speak. Daiyu paid no attention and walked into the room by herself. She saw Baoyu sitting there. He neither rose nor offered her a seat, but merely gazed at her with a foolish grin. Daiyu sat down of her own accord and gazed at Baoyu with a smile. They exchanged no greetings, spoke no words, and observed none of the customary courtesies; they simply stared into each other’s faces and grinned foolishly. The sight left Xiren utterly at a loss, but there was nothing she could do. Suddenly she heard Daiyu ask, “Baoyu, why did you fall ill?” Baoyu smiled. “I fell ill because of Miss Lin.” Xiren and Zijuan turned pale with fright and hurriedly tried to change the subject. But neither of them responded; they merely resumed their foolish smiling. Seeing this, Xiren knew that Daiyu’s present confusion was no less severe than Baoyu’s. She therefore whispered to Zijuan, “Your mistress has only just recovered. I shall have little sister Qiuwen help you take her back to rest.” Then she turned to Qiuwen and said, “Go with Sister Zijuan and escort Miss Lin back. Mind you do not talk nonsense.” Qiuwen smiled without speaking and came over to help Zijuan raise Daiyu to her feet.

p.src: Daiyu rose, gazing at Baoyu all the while, smiling and nodding repeatedly. Zijuan urged her again, “Let us go home, miss, and have a rest.” “Indeed,” said Daiyu. “It is time for me to go back.” With that, she turned and came out smiling. Still refusing the maids’ support, she walked faster than she ever normally did. Zijuan and Qiuwen hurried after her. After leaving Grandmother Jia’s courtyard, Daiyu kept walking straight ahead. Zijuan quickly took her arm and called, “This way, miss.” Still smiling, Daiyu followed her back toward the潇湘馆. When they were not far from the entrance, Zijuan exclaimed, “Amitabha! At last we are home!” Before she had finished the sentence, Daiyu suddenly pitched forward and, with a cry, vomited a mouthful of blood. Whether she lived or died remains unknown; listen to the next chapter for the outcome.
